source: REAL data, DERIVED label — peak=1: the NEXT hour's mean household load is above 1.790233 kW — the 80th percentile of hourly load over the training period (Dec 2006 – Nov 2009). DERIVED: the threshold label is ours, computed from the real readings; the dataset itself has no label. Source: Hebrail, Georges and Berard, Alice. Individual Household Electric Power Consumption [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2006. https://doi.org/10.24432/C58K54. What it is: real one-minute meter readings from one household in Sceaux (near Paris), December 2006 – November 2010, aggregated here to hours. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — redistribution of this subset is permitted with attribution. Rows: 2,075,259 published one-minute readings (25,979 with a missing value) → 34,168 clock hours with any reading, 34,151 with ≥ 45 measured minutes → 33,944 usable hourly rows (each needs the hour before, the hour after and the same hour a day earlier) (6,620 positive, base rate 19.50%). Features: for hour t: loadKw (mean active power), loadPrevKw (hour t−1), loadSameHourYesterdayKw (the target hour, one day earlier), reactiveKw, voltageV, kitchenWh / laundryWh / heaterAcWh (sub-meters 1–3, Wh in the hour); for the target hour t+1: nextHour (0–23), weekday (Mon=0 … Sun=6), month (1–12). An hour counts only if ≥ 45 of its 60 minutes were measured (the published data has ≈ 1.25% missing minutes). Split: by time — target hours before 1 December 2009 are the training split; the final twelve months (December 2009 – November 2010) are the held-out split; natural class mix (no thinning); training pool thinned evenly to 20,000 rows (class-stratified). The brain grew on 20,000 training rows only. This file: 1,500 of the 8,271 held-out rows, evenly spaced and class-stratified — 1,500 rows, 270 positive (18.00%); none were seen in growth.
